auditedSources.rightsBoundary: Existing acquisition explicitly registered catalogue/collection metadata and public pointers, not blanket rehosting rights. Item-level rights remain required.
auditedSources.recoveryDecision: This is the major legacy Chinese source pool. Recover its catalogue identities into the Chinese acquisition index, then split Bible/study items from non-Bible works and promote only rights-cleared works.
Do not scan its 67,772 documents as a Chinese collection. It may later provide translation/reference relations, but contributes zero confirmed Chinese-language works at source-manifest level.
Do not count as Chinese. PRDL manifest has no Chinese-language coverage claim. Only recover an item into zh when item metadata itself proves Chinese title/text/edition.
Potential Chinese records cannot be inferred from scale. Requires record-level language/provenance scan. Any Wikisource-derived record remains forbidden from Dawn admission.
Recover Chinese-localized Bible-world metadata for Emmaus planning; never count as 黎明書局 Chinese works merely because Chinese localization exists.
Route Chinese-localized geography to Bible-world planning, not Chinese collection admission.

keyFinding: The earlier acquisition layer DID already register a substantial Chinese-Christianity source: Yale Documentation of Chinese Christianity. The gap was not absence of Chinese acquisition intent; it was that this source remained at metadata-first/source-pool level and was never normalized into item-level Chinese canonical Works. This is the main legacy bridge to build now.
